note: Phase 11B: per-layer mixed Q8_0/Q5_1 KV storage feasibility research (whole-cache adaptive already shipped in Phase 11A; this phase investigates block/layer-level heterogeneity). RESEARCH ONLY -- experiment/mixed-q8-q5-layer-feasibility branch, never merged, never a stable CLI mode. All data is from real membrane-kv-mixed-layer invocations on this host (CPU: this host's own CPU; GPU: this host's real GTX 1650 via Vulkan), not simulated.

architecture_findings.note: Answered primarily by re-verifying Phase 4.1's own documented investigation (docs/phase4-runtime-policy.md section 3), which built and real-runtime-validated this exact per-layer mechanism (for F16/Q8_0/Q4_0) before this phase existed -- not re-derived from scratch. Independently re-confirmed here: the patch still applies to the same pinned llama.cpp commit unchanged, and the exact log line documented for the per-layer path ('attention rotation force disabled ... MEMBRANE kv_type_override') was observed firing on the new Q8_0/Q5_1 mixed context created by this phase's own probe tool.
architecture_findings.q1_type_k_v_global: By default yes -- llama_context_params.type_k/type_v are flat scalars applied to every layer. The already-tracked kv_type_override callback (patches/llama.cpp-membrane-kv-type-override.patch) overrides this per layer, per K/V, resolved once at allocation time.
architecture_findings.q2_separate_tensors_per_layer: Yes, always, in stock llama.cpp -- llama_kv_cache's constructor creates one K and one V ggml tensor per layer in a per-layer loop, independent of any MEMBRANE change.
architecture_findings.q3_per_layer_tensors_share_one_type: No, not structurally -- the ONLY place a single flat type was assumed was the two ggml_new_tensor_3d() calls inside that per-layer loop, which is exactly what the existing patch changes: layer_type_k/layer_type_v resolved via the override callback instead of the flat type_k/type_v scalar, on the same call.
architecture_findings.q4_type_stored_independently_per_tensor: Yes -- ggml_tensor::type is a per-tensor field by ggml's own design, not cache-level state. layers[il].k/v already carry their own real type after construction, with or without the override.
architecture_findings.q5_kernels_accept_heterogeneous_types: Yes, per Phase 4.1's own investigation and re-confirmed by this phase's real runs: cpy_k/cpy_v (writes), get_k/get_v (reads), and state_write_data/state_read_data (save/restore) all read the type off each layer's own tensor already, not a cached global -- no kernel-level patch was needed for the F16/Q8_0/Q4_0 case in Phase 4.1, and none was needed here either for Q8_0/Q5_1: every real run in this phase (ratio/position/sensitivity/CPU/Vulkan/ memory-pressure, all real inference through genuinely mixed contexts) completed with real, non-degenerate output and no crash.
architecture_findings.q6_limitation_scope: Allocation-time only, not compute kernels -- confirmed by construction (the patch is exactly two lines inside the KV-cache constructor) and by this phase's own real runs producing correct, non-degenerate generations across every mixed configuration tested.
known_scope_limitations_inherited_from_t: Only the standard, non-SWA, non-hybrid, non-MLA llama_kv_cache construction path honors kv_type_override (the path SmolLM2/Qwen2 use) -- iSWA/hybrid/DSA/DSv4 architectures are untouched.

Hadamard KV-rotation (a real accuracy feature) is force-disabled whenever kv_type_override is active, on every layer including ones that stay Q8 -- observed firing on every mixed context this phase created too, not just the original F16/Q8/Q4 case.

public_existing_infrastructure_findings: kv_type_override is already tracked, already-applied MEMBRANE infrastructure (Phase 4.1, patches/llama.cpp-membrane-kv-type-override.patch, auto-applied by CMakeLists.txt whenever MEMBRANE_ENABLE_LLAMA=ON) -- not a stock upstream public API, but also not a NEW third_party/llama.cpp modification this phase had to make. It was already generalized (any ggml_type per layer, not hardcoded to F16/Q8_0/Q4_0) so extending it to Q8_0/Q5_1 required zero patch changes -- only a new, simpler in-memory layer-type-array callback in a new research tool, reusing the exact same override mechanism membrane-kv-runtime (Phase 4.1) already uses.
upstream_modification_reason: Not applicable -- Section 4's stop condition was never triggered. The existing patch's kv_type_override signature (ggml_type (*)(int32_t il, bool is_v, void *ud)) is already type-generic; Q8_0/Q5_1 is just a different pair of return values through the identical mechanism Phase 4.1 already built, real-runtime-validated, and shipped as tracked infrastructure.

proof_points: One context created for the mixed config (cand_ctx), one context for the separate FP16 quality reference (ref_ctx, not a shadow of the mixed cache) -- never more.

Real log line 'attention rotation force disabled (LLAMA_ATTN_ROT_DISABLE or MEMBRANE kv_type_override)' fired exactly once per mixed-context creation, confirming kv_type_override was genuinely active.
type_map echoed back in JSON output shows real per-layer Q8_0/Q5_1 assignment matching the requested split exactly.
Real generation completed (token_identity=true, top1_preservation=1.0 on the smoke prompt) -- attention genuinely consumed both K/V dtypes in the same forward pass.
theoretical_mixed_bytes computed from the exact per-layer ggml_row_size()-based formula, no approximation.

storage_math.note: mixed_bytes = sum(Q8 layer bytes) + sum(Q5 layer bytes), using the exact same ggml_row_size()-based per-token formula every other MEMBRANE Q8/Q5 module uses (never re-derived or approximated). Exact-match proof: at ctx=8192/2048, this phase's all-Q8 special case (q8_layer_count=n_layer) produces theoretical_mixed_bytes IDENTICAL to membrane-run's own already-validated --kv q8 total at the same context size (25067520 at ctx=2048, 100270080 at ctx=8192); the all-Q5 special case likewise matches --kv q5 exactly (17694720 / 70778880). Since the mixed formula is the SAME per-layer construction summed across a heterogeneous assignment, this transitively proves the general mixed case is exact, not approximate.
storage_math.cross_check_rss_delta: A real RSS-delta measurement (before/after the mixed context's own creation, isolated from the reference context) at ctx=8192/135M/15-Q8-layers gave 87168 KiB (89,260,032 bytes) real delta vs 85,524,480 bytes theoretical -- 4.4% higher, consistent with compute-buffer/scratch allocation beyond the KV tensors themselves, corroborating (not contradicting) the exact formula.

ratio_experiments.prompt_subset: 5-prompt deterministic subset (factual_recall_1, instruction_following_1, code_reasoning_1, multistep_reasoning_2, prose_continuation_1)
ratio_experiments.note: Contiguous (early-layers-Q8) splits at 100/75/50/25/0 pct Q8. Memory decreases monotonically with fewer Q8 layers, and logit_rel_l2/delta_nll degrade monotonically and smoothly -- but top1_preservation (a discrete, threshold metric) is noisier at this 5-prompt sample size and is NOT monotonic (q8_count=15 scored better than q8_count=23 on top1 in this run). Disclosed as a real, sample-size-limited observation, not smoothed over.

layer_position_experiment.note: At IDENTICAL memory (all rows have the same theoretical_mixed_bytes), layout genuinely changes quality: reverse (late layers stay Q8) beat contiguous (early layers stay Q8) on logit_rel_l2 and delta_nll; alternating was worst overall; middle-Q8/outer-Q5 had the best delta_nll among the naive layouts. The sensitivity-based layout (see below) beat every naive layout on 2 of 3 metrics and was competitive on the third. Confirms Section 8's premise: equal memory usage does NOT imply equal quality.

layer_sensitivity_ablation.method: for each layer i, flip ONLY layer i to Q5_1, keep every other layer Q8_0, measure vs FP16 reference on the 5-prompt subset
layer_sensitivity_ablation.ranking_metric: logit_rel_l2 when that layer alone is ablated to Q5 (higher = more sensitive = should stay Q8)
layer_sensitivity_ablation.note: Ranking is NOT monotonic with layer depth (layer 27 near the end is most sensitive; layer 0 at the very start is LEAST sensitive) -- confirms Section 9's own caution not to assume early/late layers are more important.

sensitivity_based_policy_vs_naive.note: At q8_layer_count=15 (equal memory across all rows): sensitivity_based achieved the best top1_preservation (0.975) and by far the best delta_nll (0.00127, next-best was middle at 0.0089 -- ~7x worse) of every layout tested, and was competitive (2nd-best) on logit_rel_l2 (0.046 vs reverse's 0.0494). It beat random_deterministic (seed=42, same q8 count) on every metric. This clears Section 12's bar: the sensitivity-based policy outperformed naive layouts at equal memory in this run -- though on a small, 5-prompt sample, not a statistically large one.

pareto_curve.note: No single mixed point dominates all-Q8 on quality (all-Q8 has the best top1/rel_l2/nll by construction, since it is closest to the F16 reference) -- the honest research question is memory-vs-quality trade, not a free win. The curve shows a real, usable trade-off region (e.g. q8_count=15 or the sensitivity-based q8_count=15 mix recovers noticeably more quality than all-Q5 for a modest additional memory cost), not a dominant winner. No winner is forced here beyond what the numbers show.

vulkan_validation_matrix.note: VRAM peak (external nvidia-smi measurement, polled during the run) scales with theoretical KV bytes as expected (433 MiB for all-Q8/largest down to 426 MiB for all-Q5/ smallest) -- a real, physical confirmation that heterogeneous KV genuinely occupies GPU memory proportional to the mix, not a fixed/uniform allocation.

memory_pressure_result.method: --capacity-only mode (creates ONLY the candidate mixed context, never a second F16 reference context, to avoid risking real GPU OOM while probing right at the memory limit) -- raw allocation success/failure, no guard/reserve applied (unlike Phase 11A's production adaptive policy, which is deliberately more conservative).
memory_pressure_result.key_finding: At ctx=180000 (32-layer 360M, --gpu-layers all): all-Q8 (32/32) FAILS raw allocation; all-Q5 (0/32) SUCCEEDS. A mixed cache with UP TO 8 of 32 layers at Q8 (the rest Q5) ALSO SUCCEEDS at full 32/32-layer residency -- the exact same full-residency outcome whole-cache adaptive achieves only by dropping to all-Q5 (Phase 11A's own Q5_REQUIRED_FOR_FULL_RESIDENCY zone at this ctx range). 10 or more Q8 layers FAILS. This is a real, precisely-characterized YES to Section 16's central question: a mixed cache can retain some high-value layers at Q8 while matching whole-cache adaptive's full-residency memory envelope.

performance.note: Generation throughput is statistically indistinguishable across all-Q8, all-Q5, and the sensitivity-based mixed config on both backends at this small model scale -- differences are within run-to-run noise (stddev), not a systematic penalty or benefit from heterogeneous tensor types. This does NOT closely replicate Phase 4.1's F16/Q8/Q4 finding of measurably higher peak RSS for mixed configs -- this phase's mixed RSS deltas sat BETWEEN the all-Q8 and all-Q5 deltas, not above both (see cpu_validation_matrix rss_delta_cand_ctx_kb).

files_touched: CMakeLists.txt (purely additive: 2 new library/test registrations, 1 new add_subdirectory line)
tools/membrane-kv-mixed-layer/ (5 new files, self-contained, ~1170 lines total)
implementation_complexity.new_abstractions: membrane_mixed_layer_candidate_t-style plain per-layer int array (0/1 flags) plus 6 small pure functions (byte accounting, ranking assignment, 3 naive layouts) -- no new struct/class hierarchy, matching the project's existing pure-policy-module convention (adaptive_kv_policy.h/.c, compat_check.h/.c).
implementation_complexity.backend_specific_branching: None new -- the probe tool passes --gpu-layers straight into llama_model_params.n_gpu_layers exactly like the product CLI already does; no new Vulkan/CPU-specific code path was written.
implementation_complexity.llama_cpp_dependency_changes: None -- reuses the exact already-tracked patch unchanged.
implementation_complexity.maintenance_risk: LOW for the probe tool itself (self-contained, research-only, not linked into any product binary). The real maintenance risk this phase surfaces is inherited from the underlying kv_type_override patch, not new: it only covers the standard (non-SWA/hybrid/MLA) KV-cache construction path, and it force-disables Hadamard KV rotation whenever active -- both already-disclosed, pre-existing constraints (Phase 4.1), not introduced here. Productizing per-layer mixing (not attempted in this phase) would additionally need: a stable policy-assignment surface (the sensitivity ranking used here is model/prompt-set-specific, offline-computed, and was explicitly kept non-adaptive per the phase spec), a product CLI surface distinguishing it from --kv adaptive, and a much larger validation sweep than this feasibility pass performed.

tests.test_mixed_layer_policy: 14 llama-free unit tests -- exact mixed-storage sum (all-Q8, all-Q5, mixed), invalid/unsupported type fails closed, NULL/degenerate inputs, sensitivity-ranking policy (top-N-stays-Q8, q8_count clamping, invalid-permutation rejection), 3 naive layouts (contiguous/reverse/alternating, including an alternating q8_count exceeding even-index density), every-layer-assigned-exactly-once, and determinism (byte-identical repeat calls for both the byte-accounting and ranking-policy functions). All pass.

sanitizers_and_regression.result: All 5 configs green, test_mixed_layer_policy passing in every one. The one recurring failure (test_mem_guard) is a pre-existing, documented environmental flake from this dev host's own RAM pressure (unrelated to this phase -- it passed cleanly in at least one of the runs performed during this phase's own verification pass).
sanitizers_and_regression.product_regression: Purely additive change (0 existing files modified) means no regression is possible by construction; explicitly re-confirmed anyway with fresh Vulkan smoke runs of --kv native/q8/q5/adaptive, --compare-kv, and --gpu-bench --gpu-layers auto, all behaving identically to Phase 11A.

limitations: 5-prompt deterministic subset used throughout the ratio/position/sensitivity/CPU/Vulkan experiments (not the full 31-prompt derisk set) -- a real but small sample; top1_preservation in particular is noisy at this scale.
Sensitivity ranking, ratio, and position experiments were run on ONE model (SmolLM2-135M) at ONE context size (2048) -- not cross-validated on 360M or other context sizes.
The sensitivity-based policy is an OFFLINE research policy only (as the phase spec requires) -- not runtime-adaptive, not validated for generalization beyond this exact model/ prompt-set pairing.

Memory-pressure capacity results use --capacity-only (no F16 reference context, no quality metrics) specifically to avoid risking real GPU OOM -- quality-at-the-memory-boundary was NOT measured, only raw allocation success/failure.
Performance stability runs used a SINGLE prompt (not the 5-prompt subset) to keep the repeated-run sweep fast -- throughput noise across a broader prompt mix was not characterized.

Hadamard KV-rotation is disabled whenever any per-layer override is active (inherited from the Phase 4.1 patch, not new to this phase) -- every quality number in this artifact reflects that disclosed limitation, on every configuration including all-Q8.
This is a feasibility/research artifact -- no product CLI surface, no runtime policy, no merge. Q4_0/Q5_0 remain research-only and were never used anywhere in this phase.
